transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I, um... I hope I'm doing this right. 

I guess I came in because... well, I don't want to sound dramatic or be a bother, but I've just been having a really hard time lately. I keep thinking... I keep thinking it would just be better if I didn't wake up. It's awful to say that out loud, I'm sorry. But sometimes I just feel like... like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family, and to my crew at work. I lay flooring, and I just... I feel like I've ruined everything for them. 

Is... is that okay to share? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information to start with.
Have you ever felt this way or experienced a period of severe depression like this at any point in the past?

Um... I don't think I've ever had it happen in the past, not before this time, anyway. I hope I'm explaining this right. But this... this feeling I have right now, it's actually been with me for a while. About a year and two months, I think? 

It started a few months after my husband's injury. I really tried to just keep my chin up and not let it show, because I didn't want to be a burden on him while he was recovering, you know? I wanted to be strong for everyone. But it's just been lingering since then. I'm sorry, I know I probably should have come in to get help way before now... is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?

You mentioned feeling like dying is a fair punishment for what you've done to your family and coworkers; do you ever feel like you are hearing voices that aren't there, or do you have any other unusual experiences or beliefs that others might find difficult to understand?

Oh... um. I really don't want you to think badly of me, Dr. Smith. I've been so scared to mention this to anyone because I don't want them to think I'm crazy, and I really don't want to make things harder for my husband. But... well, since you asked... I guess I do. Hear things, I mean. 

It's probably just because I'm so stressed out and tired, right? But sometimes, when I'm at a job site working on a floor, or even just standing in my own kitchen at home, I hear a man's voice right behind me. He says things to me... things like, "You missed it," or "Everyone knows." It's so clear, just exactly as if someone is standing right there over my shoulder. But whenever I turn around to see who it is... nobody is there. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so strange. I usually just try to ignore it and keep working so I don't bother anyone with it. Is... is it okay that I told you that? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.

Aside from this current period of feeling down that started over a year ago, can you recall any other distinct times in your life where you felt this severely depressed or experienced these kinds of symptoms?

Um... no, I don't think so. I really don't want to waste your time with things that aren't important, but I'm pretty sure this is the first time it's been this bad. I mean, I've had normal days where I felt a little stressed or tired, like anyone else, but nothing like this... this heavy feeling, or the voices. 

I hope I'm remembering everything right. I just really want to be helpful and give you the right answers. Does that make sense? I haven't had any other times like this before my husband got hurt.
When you have days where you feel slightly better or less heavy, do those voices ever go away, or do they stay with you even when your mood is a bit lighter?

Um... well... I hope I'm explaining this right, but... yeah, they do stay. Even when I feel a little better. 

There was actually a stretch of time, maybe for a few weeks, where I was doing a bit better. I was getting up on time, eating a little more normally, and I wasn't crying all day. I really tried hard to pull myself together so I wouldn't worry my husband, you know? But... even during those weeks when my mood was lighter, I still heard the man's voice when I was at work. And... well, I also still had this feeling... this belief that my clients and the suppliers were tracking me. 

I know that probably sounds terrible, and I really don't want you to think I'm completely losing my mind. I just... I couldn't shake the feeling that they were watching me, even when I wasn't feeling so down. Is... is that the kind of thing you needed to know? I'm sorry if that's not what you were looking for.

When you feel like those clients and suppliers are watching you, do you feel like they are doing it because they are angry at you for the mistakes you believe you've made at work, or is it for some other reason?

Um... well, it's... I guess it's sort of tied to the mistakes, but it feels bigger than that. I really hope this doesn't make me sound paranoid or difficult to work with, because I always try to do a good job for everyone. But... 

Even on those days when I wasn't crying or stuck in bed, I just... I got so certain that the homeowners and the suppliers were tracking me. Like, they were using the floor patterns I was laying down, or my text messages, or even the calls for building permits to keep tabs on me. I felt like they were trying to prove that I was ruining the jobs on purpose. 

My husband tried to tell me I was just overthinking it, and I really wanted to agree with him so he wouldn't worry, but... no one could talk me out of it. It just felt so real to me. I'm sorry, I know that sounds awful, and I'm probably just letting my stress get the better of me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making things too complicated for you.

When you have these thoughts about people tracking you through your work, is there any part of you that wonders if maybe your mind is playing tricks on you, or are you completely certain that they are actually watching you?

Um... well... I want to say that maybe it's just my imagination, because I know that's what I'm supposed to think, and I really want to be reasonable about this. I don't want to be difficult or make you think I'm completely crazy. But... honestly? 

When I'm in it, even when I'm not feeling so sad or stuck in bed, I am just... I'm completely certain. It's like I can see it clearly. The way the floor patterns line up, the timing of the texts, the permit calls... it all just points to them tracking me to prove I'm ruining the jobs. My husband tries to tell me it's not real, and I try so hard to listen to him because he's so good to me, but... no one can talk me out of it. It just feels like a fact. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not the right answer, and I really hope you don't think worse of me for it. I just... I can't shake it. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm not being too much trouble.

Aside from the belief that people are tracking you through your work, have you ever felt that there were other hidden messages or secret meanings meant specifically for you in things like television programs, song lyrics, or the way objects are arranged?

Um... no, I don't think so. I really hope I'm not missing something important that I should be noticing, but... no, I haven't seen anything like that. 

I watch a little TV sometimes, mostly just home improvement shows or things like that, but I've never felt like they were talking to me or sending me secret messages. And I don't really listen to a lot of music with lyrics right now, just... maybe some quiet background noise. As for objects... well, I mean, I notice the floor patterns at work, like I said, but that's really just tied to the jobs and the suppliers. I haven't noticed anything strange with everyday objects at home or anything.

I really try to keep things as normal as possible, especially for my husband. I don't want to be seeing things everywhere. So... no, I don't think I have those kinds of thoughts. I hope that's a good thing? I'm trying really hard to be clear for you. Is that the right kind of answer?

During this past year, have you ever experienced a period of at least one week where you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable, even if you were still having those thoughts about being tracked?

Um... no, no I haven't. I really hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression, but I haven't felt high or energetic like that at all. 

Actually, it's... it's kind of been the exact opposite. Most of the time I just feel so drained, you know? Like it takes everything I have just to get out of bed or go to a job site. I definitely haven't had a whole week where I felt unusually good or full of energy. And I try really hard not to be irritable with anyone, especially my husband, because he does so much for me. I don't want to be a burden or snap at people. 

So, no, I haven't experienced anything like that. I just... I've mostly just been feeling really down, except for when I get so worried about the tracking things. I hope it's okay that I don't have that symptom? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a persistent delusional system (persecutory delusions regarding being tracked) that has lasted over a year. Importantly, the patient reports that these delusions persist even when her mood is euthymic, and she lacks the full criteria for a primary mood disorder or schizophrenia (as she denies hallucinations other than the specific voice, and lacks the disorganized speech or negative symptoms required for schizophrenia). The clinical presentation is dominated by a fixed, non-bizarre (though paranoid) belief system that is not fully explained by her depressive symptoms.

confirmed_symptoms: Fixed belief that clients and suppliers are tracking her through work-related activities like floor patterns, text messages, and building permits
Unshakeable conviction in the belief despite contrary evidence from her husband
Auditory hallucinations (hearing a man's voice commenting on her work)

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have been present for approximately 14 months (one year and two months).
additional_requirements: Absence of manic or hypomanic episodes
Delusions persist during periods of improved mood
Absence of prominent hallucinations unrelated to the delusional theme
